//: The trusted core: the modules a reader has to trust before handing this
package a page, and the evidence that nothing else needs that trust.
A module is in the core because it holds a capability the page's owner
would ask about: it reads a message from another window, sends a request
with the visitor's cookies, creates the Trusted Types policy, or writes a
value from the wire into an attribute. The primitives those modules defer
to (the escape helpers, the URL check) are in with them: the sanitizer is
only as good as `isSafeUrl`. Modules that hold a capability but stay
outside are listed under `outsideCore` with the reason each one stays
there; a module that holds one and is listed nowhere fails the gate.
`scripts/check-trusted-core.ts` counts the lines and `scripts/architecture-
rules.ts` holds every module to the capabilities written here. Numbers
are the exact current measurement, no headroom, as in complexity-budget.json.
2026-09-24 (2.1 navigation replay): 1 486 lines. message-bus.ts grows from
386 to 467 lines to retain only an accepted, token-stripped structured clone,
clone it again per local replay, fence clone accessors and origin matching
against reentrant newer messages, assign a new generation/revision, and forget
the snapshot on timeout or destroy. These 81 lines stay in the trusted ingress
owner; moving them into an uncounted helper would not reduce review scope.
2026-09-25 (H11 response identity): 1 516 lines. data-merger.ts grows
202 → 232 (+30) to capture the dispatched target, reject explicit response
identity mismatches, and fence reentrant validation. Error-field data stays valid.
The capability and its guards stay together; no trusted behavior is moved out.
2026-09-29 (ADR 0026, deprecations warn): 1 522 lines. sanitizer.ts grows 475 -> 481
for the development warning `setSanitizerDocument()` gives before 3.0 removes it: one
import and the five-line call. It is a report, never a behaviour; the slot is written
the same way whether or not it prints. `types/dev-warning.ts` is reviewed below.
2026-10-02 (PHD-19, the sanitizer settles): 1 557 lines. sanitizer.ts grows 481 -> 500
and url-validator.ts 44 -> 60. `sanitizeHtml` parses, sanitises and writes again until
a pass changes nothing: an unwrapped unknown tag can leave a tree no parser produces,
and the consumer's `innerHTML` rebuilds it, so the string handed back must already be
the rebuilt one (the loop, its cap and the warning when it does not settle: 19 lines).
`isSafeUrl` reads a scheme through whitespace and control characters as DOMPurify does,
so `java script:` is refused (the gap class, its reading and the comments saying why:
20 lines, less the 4 of the dangerous-scheme pattern that reading made redundant).
Both answer findings of the daily property exploration (ADR 0016, addendum); no trusted
behavior is moved out.

One statement, no capability, module or validation path changes. The exact line ceiling grows 2 064 -> 2 065 by this measured difference. 2026-10-28 (2.2.1, the sanitizer writes what it cleaned): the same nine modules measure 2 083 lines, with no headroom. sanitizer.ts grows 501 -> 519 (+18). `sanitizeHtml` read `template.content`, cleaned it and wrote the template back; linkedom's `content` is a copy of the template's children, so with a linkedom document every call returned its input. It now reads `content` once (one statement and three comment lines at the call) and writes those nodes through an element of their own document (`serialize`: eight lines, a five-line header and a blank line), refusing with the environment error when there is no such element or it does not hold them. No capability, module or allow-list changes; the jsdom output is byte-identical on the corpus and 30 000 fuzz inputs under three policies. The exact line ceiling grows 2 065 -> 2 083 by this measured difference.

lines.why: Measured on 2026-09-11, `wc -l` over the eight modules: 386 + 95 + 202 + 68 + 443 + 68 + 48 + 44. A thousand lines is about what one reader holds in one sitting and was the size this core set out to be; this is not it, so the number is a finding, not a target met. What makes it large is not a second responsibility: 133 of the sanitizer's 443 lines are the allow-lists a reader has to read anyway (which tags, which attributes), and about 130 of the bus's 386 are the queue that commits token verdicts in arrival order (ADR 0004) — moving either into a file of its own would leave the reader the same lines in two places. 2026-09-10 the measurement was 1 393 (1 087 without blank and comment lines). 2026-09-11 (Z28): 1 354, after the core's own mutation run showed which lines no test could reach — the merger's redundant abort-signal check, its unreachable collection-slug fallback and the `try { encodeURIComponent }` probes (the one encoding call that builds the path refuses a lone surrogate by itself), the bus's generation checks that the next boundary repeats, its `sendReady` early return, the unreachable `attachedTarget` guard in the source check and the array-with-compaction queue (now a linked list), the escape helpers' empty-string fast paths, the validator's empty check before trimming and the guard `isExternalHttpUrl` implied by its own patterns, and the sanitizer's `insertBefore` loop (now `replaceWith`). `binding-writer.ts` (196 lines) was the obvious ninth candidate; it is outside because it holds no capability — its two exits are `applyAttributeBinding` and a renderer, both held by the gates below — and `docs/audit.md` reads it first after the core for that reason. 2026-09-14 (2.0.1): 1 356. LP0409 said the 1.x `compat` policy kept `name`, which it never did; the sanitizer now asks whether `compat` would have kept it before reporting, one condition on the line that already reported and two comment lines saying why (sanitizer.ts 443 → 445; 1 032 lines without blank and comment lines, unchanged). 2026-09-17 (2.0.2): 1 364. The document `setSanitizerDocument()` supplies moved from a module variable to a registry symbol on the realm, because every package entry is its own bundle with its own copy of this module, and a document set through the root never reached `lexicalToHtml` from `/lexical`, which then returned unsanitised HTML on the server (sanitizer.ts 445 → 453: the symbol, its three-line slot type, and three comment lines saying why). 2026-09-17 (2.0.3): 1 383. dependencies.src/core/diagnostics.ts: Wraps a consumer's logger so a diagnostic that throws cannot become a second failure; 38 lines, no capability.
dependencies.src/core/protocol-version.ts: The protocol version constant the `ready` handshake announces, and the capability table read off the wire (ADR 0010); the bus takes only the constant.
dependencies.src/core/thenable.ts: Assimilates a thenable a synchronous callback returned, so a rejected promise from consumer code does not surface as unhandled; 14 lines.
dependencies.src/schema/parser.ts: Validates fieldSchemaJSON entry by entry, including observed v2 relation targets, Blocks records and named tabs. Its normalized schema supplies renderer typing and the legacy plan; it grants no authorization. URL/ID refusal, bounded document copying and response identity remain in the counted legacy-population primitive. Its existing operation-wide node counter also charges each copied polymorphic target; unrelated opaque metadata is not traversed.
dependencies.src/types/dev-warning.ts: One development warning per key and process, outside production only, keys on `globalThis`; the sanitizer calls it from `setSanitizerDocument()` alone. No capability: it reads `NODE_ENV` and writes `console.warn`, and a console that throws is swallowed.
dependencies.src/security/sanitizer-report.ts: LP0409, the once-per-name warning that the strict sanitizer removed an attribute the 1.x default kept. A report, never a behaviour: the attribute stays removed whether or not the warning prints.

src/client/preview-focus.ts.why: The admin-side reporter for reveal tier 2: posts `{ type, field }` to the preview window at its exact origin, never `'*'`. It runs in the admin, not in the page, and carries a field name, never a value.

src/core/loader.ts.why: The static-delivery bootstrap: one `<script>` whose `src` and `integrity` are build-time constants the generator prepends. Nothing from the page or the wire reaches the URL.

src/core/strategy-runner.ts.why: Morphs a fragment the page's own server rendered into its boundary, parsed into a `<template>` first. Sanitising it would strip the page's own legitimate markup; the sink inventory records it as `trusted-origin`.

src/core/structural-applier.ts.why: Parses an item the sanitizer already cleaned into a `<template>` so it can be adopted; `sanitised` in the sink inventory, and inert twice over.

src/field-types/array.ts.why: Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `sanitizeHtmlWithPolicy()` and nothing else, per site in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/html.ts.why: Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `sanitizeHtmlWithPolicy()` and nothing else, per site in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/rich-text.ts.why: Renderer; every site feeds `trustedHtml()` a string the sanitizer produced with the instance's policy, including the one that parses a sanitised string into a detached clone.

src/field-types/text.ts.why:
Renderer; feeds `trustedHtml()` from `escapeAndLinebreak()`, which escapes before it inserts `
`; `escaped` in the sink inventory.

src/field-types/upload.ts.why: Renderer; builds one `<a>` from `escapeHtmlAttribute()` and `escapeHtml()` around a URL that passed `isSafeUrl`; `escaped` in the sink inventory.

src/fragment/handler.ts.why: POST to the page's own fragment endpoint with `credentials: 'same-origin'`; the JSON that comes back is validated before any of it reaches a boundary (ADR 0011).

src/fragment/route.ts.why: GET of the page's own route, same-origin, `cache: 'no-store'`; the HTML is parsed by `DOMParser` into an inert document, then morphed. The server that answers is the one that rendered the page.

src/plugins/built-in/document-save.ts.why: Opt-in plugin: on a document event it POSTs to the revalidation URL the consumer configured, or reloads the page. Neither runs unless the page author registered it.

src/security/preview-session.ts.why: Server-side: forwards exactly one named cookie to `<serverURL>/api/<users>/me`. Never in a page; the browser runtime does not contain it.

src/server/preview.ts.why: Server-side draft read through the REST API, with the headers the authorized context carries. Never in a page.

src/doctor/probe.ts.why: `pll doctor`, a maintainer tool run from a shell against a deployment; redirects are reported, not followed, and the body is capped.
